headline: Elon Musk confirmed that TSMC is in talks to join his Terafab chip project, which so far has Intel as its only named partner.
score_reason: Confirmed talks between the world's largest chipmaker and Musk's chip venture, but nothing is agreed and the structure is speculation.
importance_line: A TSMC-run plant serving only Tesla, SpaceX and xAI would change who supplies Musk's cars, rockets and AI models with chips and could push Intel out of the project, but Musk himself calls it just discussions.
summary: Tom's Hardware reports, citing Tim Culpan's Culpium newsletter, that TSMC and Terafab, Musk's plan for a chip plant supplying Tesla, SpaceX and xAI exclusively, are discussing a deal under which TSMC would build and run the fab; Musk confirmed on X that there are "just discussions, but something may come of it", and TSMC has not commented. Intel is so far the only named partner, slated to supply its 14A production process, and Tom's Hardware notes that a TSMC role could displace it, while the ownership models being floated remain the newsletter's analysis rather than anything official.
notes: Culpium (2 Oct) first reported the talks; Musk's confirmation came 3 Oct. Source written as 'X reports, citing Y' per the credit rule.
